rationale.authz_guard: Comparison forms `== request.user` / `request.user ==` / `!=` variants come from DRF's documented custom permission `IsOwnerOrReadOnly` (`return obj.owner == request.user`, api-guide/permissions); both operand orders are listed because the rule is a plain substring match. The `.id` and `.pk` forms cover the equivalent `obj.user_id == request.user.id` / `.pk` spelling (Django docs use pk and id interchangeably). `== self.request.user` / `!=` cover the class-based-view spelling; the operator-after forms (`request.user ==`) already match `self.request.user ==` as a suffix, so only the operator-before forms needed a `self.` duplicate. Keyword-scoping forms `user=request.user`, `owner=request.user`, `user_id=request.user.id` and the `self.request.user` duplicates come from the DRF generic-views idiom `serializer.save(owner=self.request.user)` and the shortcut idiom `get_object_or_404(Model, pk=pk, owner=request.user)`: a kwarg appears in the call's code, so it is legitimate guard text. `check_object_permissions` is the DRF view method the docs say to call yourself when writing custom views (`self.check_object_permissions(request, obj)`); `has_object_permission` is the object-level hook of a permission class; `djangoobjectpermissions` is DRF's built-in object-level permission class (lower-cased identifier as it appears in `@permission_classes([...])`). `djangomodelpermissions`, `isadminuser`, `permission_required`, `has_perm(`, `has_perms(`, `user.is_staff`, `user.is_superuser`, `staff_member_required` are model-level / role checks from topics/auth/default and DRF permissions; they were classified as authorization to stay consistent with the reference pack, which put `roles_required`, `current_user.is_admin` and `current_user.has_role` in authz_guard. `user.is_staff` (not `is_staff`) so the token requires a user object and is not tripped by an unrelated attribute.
rationale.authn_only: `request.user` (also matches `self.request.user`) is the docs' logged-in user object and proves nothing about the object being read; `request.auth` is DRF's authentication context (api-guide/requests). `authentication` covers `authentication_classes`, `SessionAuthentication`, `TokenAuthentication` and the `@authentication_classes` decorator (api-guide/views). `authenticate(` is `django.contrib.auth.authenticate`, credential verification. `permission_classes` and `check_permissions` are DRF's view-level permission list and the method that runs it; in the docs the typical list is `[IsAuthenticated]`, which is login only, so they must not suppress. When the list contains DjangoObjectPermissions the authz_guard token matches separately. `loginrequiredmixin` is the CBV login mixin (lower-cased identifier). `user_passes_test` runs an arbitrary predicate on the user, not on the object, so it is evidence, not proof of ownership. Cross-slot rule checked: no authz_guard value is a substring of any of these.
rationale.lock_guard: `=f(`, ` f(`, `(f(`, `models.f(` are the positions in which an `F(...)` call appears in the docs' 'Avoiding race conditions using F()' section (`reporter.stories_filed = F("stories_filed") + 1`, `update(stories_filed=F("stories_filed") + 1)`), where the docs state the database rather than Python applies the write. A bare `f(` was rejected because it is a suffix of every call whose name ends in f (`stuff(`). `skip_locked` is a `select_for_update()` argument from ref/models/querysets; `select_for_update`, `atomic`, `transaction` and `savepoint` are inherited from _base and were not duplicated.
rationale.allowlist_guard: topics/forms/modelforms says it is 'strongly recommended that you explicitly set all fields that should be edited using the fields attribute', so writing through a form is an allow-list by construction: `is_valid(`, `cleaned_data`, `form(request.post` (the docs' `f = ArticleForm(request.POST)` — the docs also show `f.save()` without an explicit `is_valid()`, so the instantiation itself is needed) and `form(data=`. DRF serializers likewise declare fields: `validated_data` (the docs' `create(self, validated_data)` / `update(self, instance, validated_data)` bodies, which loop `setattr` over validated_data), `get_serializer(` (generic-views), `read_only_fields` (serializers Meta). `update_fields=` is `save(update_fields=[...])` from ref/models/instances, an explicit list of fields on the write itself. `fields=[` / `fields=(` (no spaces) are the `modelform_factory(Book, fields=[...])` spelling; the spaced `fields = [` form is inherited from _base. `get_form(` is the FormView / ModelFormMixin accessor.
rationale.positive_guard: `min_value=0` / `min_value=1` are the IntegerField / DecimalField / FloatField bound from ref/forms/fields, which the docs say maps to `MinValueValidator` (hence `minvaluevalidator(`). `positiveintegerfield`, `positivesmallintegerfield`, `positivebigintegerfield` are the model field family that ref/models/fields says 'must be either positive or zero'. `>= 1`, `<= 0`, `< 0` are the comparison forms of a `clean_<field>()` bound (`if value < 0: raise ValidationError`); _base only has the `> 0` / `>= 0` / `> 1` orientations. `< 1` was rejected because it is a substring of `< 10`, `< 100` (upper bounds).
rationale.mass_assign_signal: `request.post` and `request.body` are the HttpRequest client-data attributes from ref/request-response; `.dict()` is `QueryDict.dict()`, the documented way to turn POST into a plain dict (the wholesale form `Model.objects.create(**request.POST.dict())`). `request.data` and `request.query_params` are DRF's parsed body and query string (api-guide/requests). Values sit in signal_text, which includes literals, so `.dict()` with its parentheses is safe.
rationale.qty_terms: `num_` is the counter prefix the docs use in F() and aggregation examples (`num_employees`, `num_chairs`, `num_books`); `votes` is the tutorial's counter (`choice.votes`). Both are count-like operands for the unchecked-quantity and TOCTOU rules. Checked disjoint from price_terms.
rationale.price_terms: `cost`, `fee`, `credit`, `payment`, `funds` are general money words; Django's own docs only use `price`, which _base already has, so this slot is the least docs-grounded and is noted as such in the pack. `discount` was rejected because it contains _base's qty term `count`.
rationale.orm_read_calls: `get_object_or_404` / `aget_object_or_404` from topics/http/shortcuts are the docs' single-object-by-id read in views. `last`, `earliest`, `latest` and the async `aget`, `afirst`, `alast`, `aearliest`, `alatest` are the QuerySet methods ref/models/querysets lists as returning a single object (`first` is in _base). `get_object` is DRF's GenericAPIView detail read (`self.get_object()` in generic-views); the permissions guide says object-level checks happen only when `check_object_permissions` runs, which is an authz_guard value, so a method that calls get_object with an id parameter and no such token is a legitimate candidate. `get` itself was rejected (see left_out).
rationale.dyn_write_calls: `update` is `QuerySet.update(**kwargs)` (and dict.update / QueryDict.update); `update_or_create` takes a `defaults=` mapping (ref/models/querysets). Both write a mapping wholesale when handed one. `setattr` is inherited.
rationale.mapping_iter_calls: `lists` is `QueryDict.lists()`, documented as 'Like items(), except it includes all values, as a list' (ref/request-response). `model_to_dict` is django.forms.models' instance-to-mapping helper, the Django analogue of _base's `to_dict`.
rationale.commit_calls: Django runs in autocommit mode (topics/db/transactions), so there is no explicit commit call in ordinary view code: the ORM write is the commit. `save`, `delete` (ref/models/instances), `update`, `create`, `bulk_create`, `bulk_update` (ref/models/querysets) and their async forms `asave`, `adelete`, `aupdate`, `acreate` are the writes the TOCTOU rule should see after a check. `perform_create`, `perform_update`, `perform_destroy` are DRF's save/deletion hooks (generic-views) that wrap `serializer.save()` / `instance.delete()`.
rationale.exec_calls: `raw` is `Manager.raw("SELECT ...")` (topics/db/sql); `RawSQL` is the expression `RawSQL("select ...", params)` from ref/models/expressions; both carry the SQL text in the call's code where the exec_sql_kw slots are searched. `executemany` is the DB-API cursor method exposed by Django's cursor wrapper; it is not on the topics/db/sql page (verified) and is included on the same footing as the reference pack's sqlite3 entry.
rationale.sql_read_kw / sql_write_kw / sql_delete_: No additions: Django adds no SQL keywords of its own; SELECT / INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE are inherited.
rationale.id_param_exact: `pk` is DetailView's `pk_url_kwarg` default and DRF's `lookup_field` default; `slug` is `slug_url_kwarg`'s default; `uuid` is the `<uuid:...>` URL path converter. _base has `id`.
rationale.id_param_suffix: `_pk`, `_slug`, `_uuid` are the suffix forms of the same names when a URL kwarg is prefixed with the model (`<int:question_pk>`); `_id` is inherited.

left_out.reason: dict.get / request.POST.get / request.GET.get / cache.get share the exact call name; every method with an id parameter would become a candidate. Same judgement as the reference pack; the async aget has no such collision and is included.

Documented as the race-safe replacement for check-then-create, so listing them as the TOCTOU write would flag the docs' own fix. update_or_create is kept only in dyn_write_calls for its defaults= mapping.

The docs' create() takes explicit kwargs (`Person.objects.create(first_name=...)`); as a dynamic-write trigger it would fire on every ordinary insert that also touches request.POST. Kept in commit_calls where it is unambiguously a DB write.
obj.save() follows almost every explicit field assignment; as a dynamic-write trigger it is far too broad. Kept in commit_calls.

Lower-cased request.GET is a prefix of request.get_host / get_full_path / get_signed_cookie / get_json; a substring value would misfire on every one of them. DRF's request.query_params covers the query-string mapping without the collision.
